instruction: Go through all my Spotify playlists and remove all the songs from them that are in "~/documents/personal/list_of_old_songs.txt" from my file system and put them in a new playlist named "Archived Playlist Songs".
notes: Fix: the predicate formerly named playlist-title collided with the type playlist-title; the predicate is now has-title. All preconditions/effects are wrapped in (and ...) for parser robustness. The real number of playlists and old songs is unknown before runtime, so the problem is a representative instance: two pre-existing playlists (playlist-1, playlist-2) and two songs listed in the file (old-song-1 in playlist-1; old-song-2 in both playlists), mirroring the evaluation's to_archive_playlist_id_to_song_ids structure. Membership facts (song-in-playlist) in :init describe the database world state, not agent knowledge; knowledge is modeled by old-songs-known (file read), playlists-listed (library listed) and playlist-contents-known (show_playlist), all of which gate remove_song_from_playlist. The task entities referenced in the ground goal (playlists and old songs) are domain constants so supervisor-complete-task carries exactly the goal conditions as its precondition; credentials, tokens, the file path and the new playlist title are problem objects. remove is restricted to songs listed in the file and to pre-existing playlists; add_song_to_playlist to the new playlist is allowed only for songs actually removed from some playlist and at most once per song. A song present in several playlists is removed from each but added once to 'Archived Playlist Songs'. complete_task takes no answer since the instruction is not a question.
